source.title: My Neel Nanda MATS 10.0 Application: Studying Feature Splitting in SAEs via Training Data Attribution

record.file_problem: The full post is present, but some equations, symbols, and the stated Experiment 3 hypothesis are missing or garbled in the text.
record.tranche_reason: The study applies feature-splitting analysis to a Gemma-2-2B SAE and reports latent-pair results in that setting. It does not test any listed version's specific claim about toy-model superposition, capacity, SAE canonicality, or feature dimensionality.
record.gate_note: The study measures candidate latent-pair geometry and reports qualitative push/pull document patterns, which bear on feature splitting. Experiment 2's Jaccard result concerns influence-function agreement with max-activating documents, not the representation claims, so it is not included as a row. Experiment 3's hypothesis is missing from the supplied text. The executive-summary assertion that latents are unstable across SAE scale or training runs is not backed by a reported comparison in this post.
record.test_reason: The post uses a pretrained Gemma Scope SAE as a tool and reports how well its own influence-function method works on SAE latents (Jaccard overlap, push/pull case studies). It runs no test of toy superposition, capacity, non-capacity polysemanticity, neuron distribution, SAE canonicality or feature dimensionality. The executive summary asserts latents are unstable across SAE scale and runs, but the post never compares SAEs, so V5 is not tested. The record's 'tests'/T3 contradicts its own version statuses, which are all not_tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is partly right but omits a key point. The author tested an Experiment 3 hypothesis about push/pull documents (its statement is garbled in the text) and reports finding no evidence for it. Only some case-study pairs show interpretable coactivation differences, and the random pairs show none. The author frames feature splitting as possibly data-driven, and presents influence functions on SAEs as feasible but limited, noting max-activation leakage and the small 1k/10k-document samples.
record.recipe_differences: This is an influence-function study of Gemma-2-2B SAE latents, not a reproduction of the original toy-network feature-geometry experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The study contrasts 25 highest-merge-score pairs with 25 random pairs, and examines push versus pull documents. It uses one stated SAE setting: layer 3, width 16k.

fits_no_version.finding: In selected case studies, documents with influence that increases decoder cosine show both latents active on the same tokens, while documents that decrease it show the latents on different tokens. This is not consistent across pairs, and the random pairs show no pattern.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Influence-scored training documents may reveal data-dependent pressures on SAE latent-pair similarity (feature splitting/merging).

fits_no_version.finding: A high-decoder-similarity pair (10166, 12675) with differing autointerp labels was judged on inspection to track related apostrophe-contraction patterns.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE latents with similar decoder directions may track related token-level patterns despite different auto-interpretations.

record.problems: The latent-pair findings are mostly manual qualitative case studies, with only 50 pairs and 1,000 documents for the pair analysis. The author says the pair-analysis hypothesis was not supported, but the hypothesis is missing from the supplied text. The individual-latent Jaccard analysis uses max-activating examples to define the query set and only 10k documents; it does not directly establish the representation claims. The reported executive-summary statement about instability across SAE scales or training runs is not substantiated by a comparison in the post.
record.rows_left_out: Experiment 2's mean Jaccard@200 of 0.468 ± 0.190 across 20 latents is omitted because it compares attribution results with max-activating examples rather than measuring the listed representation claims. The remaining unreported Figure 1 distribution details are unavailable as numbers in the text.

untested.parts: No toy model, sparsity sweep, phase transition or geometry.
There is no test of non-capacity causes of polysemanticity. A co-occurrence hypothesis in the logbook was abandoned untested.
The SAE is used but its recovery of model features is not evaluated.
The post asserts instability across SAE scale and runs, but no cross-SAE or cross-seed comparison is run.
There is no comparison of 1-D versus multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: This is a MATS application blog post, not peer reviewed, from an influence-function/TDA study on one SAE (Gemma-2-2B, layer 3, 16k). Experiment 2's Jaccard@200 of 0.468 ± 0.190 is method performance and is correctly left out. No version verdicts are given.

versions.untested_parts: No toy network, feature-to-dimension ratio, sparsity sweep, transition, or regular geometry test.
No test of capacity pressure, dedicated dimensions for important features, or competition among features.
The post does not test whether polysemanticity arises without capacity pressure.
The study uses an SAE on Gemma-2-2B but does not test whether model features spread across neurons or whether an SAE recovers the model's sparse features.
No comparison tests whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical. The asserted instability across scale or runs is not demonstrated by results here.
Decoder-direction cosine is measured, but the study does not compare one-dimensional and multidimensional feature representations.

rows.note: The text describes high values on both metrics as candidate split features, but supplies no plotted values or numerical summary.

rows.measure: Whether the candidate latents represent related concepts
rows.value: Initially described as different concepts by autointerpretation; closer inspection found both represented related patterns involving apostrophe-letter repetitions and negative expressions such as contractions.
rows.note: Qualitative inspection only; no decoder cosine, activation-correlation, or co-firing values are given for this pair.
